findings.title: Arena floor is a seamed, unbounded grey void
findings.where: Arena screen: the entire ground plane around the car; straight tiling seams form a faint grid across the field and no wall, prop or decal appears anywhere in frame
findings.problem: The surface is one low-contrast noise texture whose tile seams read as straight vertical/horizontal lines; with no boundary, cover, markings or stains in view, the combat space is an empty grey plane with a single small car in the middle.
findings.why: Players read arena extent and their own speed from landmarks and surface detail; the seams make the texture look broken, and the void gives nothing to judge distance, velocity or the fight ring against, so the mode feels like a test scene rather than an arena.
findings.fix: Hide the seams with offset/rotated tiles or a crack-and-decal overlay, then dress the ring: a barrier wall or tire-stack boundary at the play edge, 4-6 props (barrels, containers, corner stacks), and painted ground decals (center circle, skid arcs, oil stains) so extent and motion are readable at a glance.

findings.title: City POIs are unlabeled chevrons on a street-less plain
findings.where: City screen: inside the gate ring; saturated chevron markers hovering over flat grey box buildings, with the only key being a ~8px four-swatch legend pinned to the bottom-right corner
findings.problem: Services are raw colored chevrons (green/blue/orange/red) with no name plates, and all four share one identical shape; buildings sit directly on cracked noise with no streets, curbs or lots connecting them, so the markers float instead of being placed.
findings.why: At driving speed the player cannot tell a job board from a garage without cross-referencing a corner legend that is too small to read while steering; without a street network the 'city' reads as placeholder icons on a texture, not a place to navigate.
findings.fix: Lay dark asphalt street strips with curb lines connecting the buildings and the gate, and attach a small label plate (color swatch + name, e.g. 'Jobs', 'Garage') above each marker that fades in within ~40m or on hover; promote the legend into the left HUD stack at readable row height.

findings.title: Route progress renders as an unstyled debug slider
findings.where: Road screen: top-center, directly beneath the 'En route to Albany · 150mi remaining' chip
findings.problem: The journey meter is a plain black rounded track with a lone white knob at the left end: no progress fill, no origin/destination marks, no distance ticks, and no mileage on the bar itself.
findings.why: It is the primary courier feedback for long drives; as a bare range-input it communicates fraction-complete and distance-left only through the text chip above, and it is the single most obviously unfinished UI element on the screen.
findings.fix: Rebuild it as a route instrument: origin and destination ticks with city abbreviations at each end, an accent-color fill running from origin to a small car glyph, quarter-distance ticks, and the remaining-mi number riding the fill edge; give the track a 1px light inner border so it reads over both shoulder and asphalt.

findings.title: Settings literals shipped as permanent HUD chips
findings.where: Arena and Road screens: bottom-right corner, two stacked chips reading 'Reduced flash: off' and 'Reduced shake: off'
findings.problem: Two grey chips expose raw options state ('off') during play; they share no panel, icon or accent language with the rest of the HUD and occupy a corner otherwise reserved for gameplay feedback.
findings.why: Visible settings literals read as a debug build and train players to scan past that corner; they also add two dead lines of text to every combat frame, diluting the corners that carry real telemetry.
findings.fix: Move both options into the pause/settings menu; if an in-HUD reminder is required, show a single small icon (crossed bolt / stabilized glyph) only while a reduction is active, docked into the radar panel's header row with a hover tooltip.

findings.title: Constructor collapses into half-empty voids with flat row hierarchy
findings.where: Constructor screen: left column below the key-hint line (roughly y=650 downward) and right column below the LEGALITY panel; also the 16 armour+weapon rows in the left list and the small schematic inside the SUBCOMPACT panel
findings.problem: Both columns stop at about 60% of viewport height leaving large black dead regions; armour and weapon rows are separated only by a thin yellow gutter so they read as one undifferentiated 16-row stack; the top-view car schematic fills only a small fraction of its panel.
findings.why: This is the player's first authoring screen; the dead space makes the build feel unbuilt, and without group headers or a dominant preview the player cannot see at a glance what costs weight versus what mounts where while editing.
findings.fix: Make the left list a full-height scroll region with sticky group headers (IDENT / ARMOUR / MOUNTS) and stronger selected/hover row states; scale the top-view schematic to fill its panel with labeled mount slots and a FRONT tag; pin the key-hint line to a footer bar spanning both columns so the bottom edge reads deliberate.
